issues.failure_explanation: In the proof the interaction-picture operator is written with A only, and the calculation uses f=(i partial_t-H)u*. When B is nonzero, u* solves (i partial_t-H-B(t))u*=f, so the displayed identity F(v)=||u-u*||_{X_H}^2 is false. The correct identity is F(v)=N(u)^2, with the gamma=2 lower bound coming from the time-dependent norm equivalence, not from the time-independent one.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry A+B(t) through the interaction-picture calculation, use f=(i partial_t-H-B(t))u*, conclude F(v)=N(u)^2, and then apply Theorem th: XX0 XX equality part (i) for B=0 and part (ii) for B nonzero.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the proof covers only B=0; the stated gamma=2 estimate for genuinely time-dependent bounded perturbations is not justified by the displayed computation.
issues.title: Proof of the H^1 variational corollary drops the bounded perturbation B(t)
issues.why_classification: The needed time-dependent norm equivalence is already proved; the repair is a contained correction of the displayed algebra and citation, with no change to the statement, constants type, or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: Since H=H_0+A, the adjoint form S* is built from i partial_t-H_0-(A+B(t)), whereas S_0* is built from i partial_t-H_0. Thus, in the antilinear-form sense used for these operators, S*=S_0*-(A+B(t)), and the equivalent equation should contain Id-(S_0*)^{-1}(A+B(t)). The displayed plus signs and the Id+ equation describe a different, sign-flipped problem.

issues.failure_explanation: The inclusion C_c^\infty(I,H) subset Y_{H_0} is false: membership in Y_{H_0} requires membership in X_{H_0}, i.e. a weak (i partial_t-H_0) derivative in L^2. For example, with H_0=-Delta and w(t)=eta(t) phi with eta smooth compactly supported but phi in L^2 not in H^2, (i partial_t-H_0)w is not in L^2, so w is not in Y_{H_0}. Consequently e^{-itH}w need not be an admissible test function for S* as the converse computation assumes.

issues.failure_explanation: The section's standing hypothesis includes B(t), and Duhamel for i partial_t u=H_0u+(A+B(t))u+f moves the term i integral e^{-i(t-s)H_0}(A+B(s))u(s) ds to the left side. The displayed functional contains only Au, and the proof identifies it with (S_0*)^{-1}S*u even though S* was defined with H=H_0+A and B(t). For nonzero B the stated minimizer and error equivalence concern the equation with B removed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Au by (A+B(t))u in the Duhamel integral, equivalently insert B(s)u(s), and make the same replacement in the proof identity relating the functional to (S_0*)^{-1}S*u.
issues.overall_effect: Corollary cor:L2 and its L^2 error equivalence are unsupported, and as stated false for the intended time-dependent problem, except in the special case B=0.
issues.title: The L^2 least-squares functional omits the time-dependent potential B(t)
issues.why_classification: The omitted term is the already assumed bounded perturbation; inserting it restores the stated constants and guarantee without any new estimate, lemma, or change of scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: An element $u \in \Ltwosp{J, \HHilb}$ is said to be a weak solution

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem says u* is in X_{-Delta} and solves the equation in the sense of Definition def: definition weak solution with J=R. That definition requires u to belong to L^2(J,H), while X_H was introduced for the finite interval I=(0,T). For the homogeneous equation here the solution is norm conserving, so for nonzero u_0 its L^2(R,H) norm is infinite; hence it cannot be a weak solution on R in the stated sense.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate u* as the standard mild/strong solution given by the unitary propagator for -Delta+V(t), equivalently as the weak solution on every bounded time interval, and keep v*=e^{-it Delta}u*; the proved estimates then apply verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: The regularity statement is formally attached to an ill-fitting solution notion on the whole line; the later proof establishes the intended pointwise polynomial time-regularity bounds only through a propagator/strong-solution interpretation.
issues.title: Time-regularity theorem invokes the finite-time weak-solution class on J=R
issues.why_classification: Only the solution notion on R needs the standard propagator/localized formulation; the regularity conclusion, growth rate, and later numerical motivation are preserved without a new argument.
